messages.text:
I need a control plot:

- please make an un-tiled version of the current ECal (with the full silicon slab over the entire sectors, even if that could not be built in reality)
- repeat the same 10k electron sample for this 
- overlay the sigma(R)/R so that we see how much of this resolution degradation comes from the readout module tiling

I’ll make an isolated control geometry with continuous silicon across each ECAL sector, then rerun the same 10,000 primary inputs with 12 threads and the same seeds. I’ll verify the geometry differences before running it and overlay the two angular response-width curves with paired statistical uncertainties.

I’m using the repository’s detector validation workflow and the ACTS Spack skill for this control. The environment preflight reports changed setup fingerprints, so I’ll verify the installed runtime before building. I’ll also record exactly which inactive silicon gaps the control fills.

The completed plots and results are already in [draft PR #135](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/135). I’m checking the remaining six-file metadata update against that published revision.

Automatic approval review rejected the final push because it could not establish authorization for the external destination and complete payload. I’ll verify the exact remote and diff before retrying.

Repeated the **same 10,000 electrons with 12 threads**. All events passed readback; 385 GiB remains free.

![Tiled versus continuous silicon response widths]([redacted]

| Response width | Tiled | Continuous silicon |
|---|---:|---:|
| Absolute η bins | 28–56% | 9–16% |
| Folded φ interior | 23–25% | 3.7–4.1% |
| Near sector seams | ≈110% | ≈27% |

The control fills module, guard and service gaps and requires support cuts. Sector seams remain. Bars show 95% paired-bootstrap intervals.
